card.name: Teacher and student lineage in philosophy history
card.fires_on: Words in biographies of ancient thinkers and their schools, such as 'his' or 'and' after a master's name, where a disciple or follower is likely next.

modes.label: Pronoun about a philosopher
modes.description: 'his' or 'other' in biographical text about a thinker's successor, enemies or pupils.
modes.example: Plato soon distinguished him above all his<< other>> disciples.

modes.label: Master and pupil names
modes.description: A teacher's name or a linking word between two thinkers of one school.
modes.example: While the differences between Confucius<< and>> Mencius are acknowledged

modes.label: Source citations
modes.description: Parts of classical or hadith source names in references.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words for disciples, followers and teacher-student relations.
card.plain: It lights up in histories of philosophers when the next word is likely to be about their students or followers.
